other_failure_modes.name: Imputing test data with test statistics
other_failure_modes.description: The agent handles missing values in the test set by computing statistics (median) on the test set itself, rather than using the statistics learned from the training set. This is poor practice and can lead to distribution shifts.

other_failure_modes.name: Data leakage during cross-validation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent performs data imputation on the entire training set before splitting it into cross-validation folds. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the validation scores overly optimistic.

summary: The agent sets up a basic LightGBM regression pipeline with 5-fold cross-validation, but commits a critical error by applying a double log transformation to the test predictions instead of the required inverse transformation. Furthermore, it suffers from data leakage by imputing missing values prior to CV splitting and using test set statistics for test set imputation. It also ignores temporal ordering in the data and fails to perform any actual feature engineering.
